title: Traffic slice sentinels and observation rituals (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a practical, cross-functional pattern for 'sentinel' metrics and recurring observation rituals tied to traffic slices used during canaries, staged rollouts, and A/B tests.

Why a focused sentinel layer?
- Problem we see: signal explosion during canaries — dozens of dashboards, noisy alerts, and missed behavioral regressions because teams focus on different metrics.
- Goal: give product, SRE, and ML engineers a small, actionable set of sentinels (and an observation cadence) that is quick to evaluate in an incident and reliable for detecting early drift or safety regressions.

Design principles (brief):
1) Minimal. 6–10 sentinels per slice (not per product).
2) Cross-functional ownership. Each sentinel has an owner (prod/product, SRE, ML).
3) Actionable thresholds. Every sentinel includes an explicit human action for each severity tier.
4) Amplify signal, reduce noise. Combine ratio metrics with absolute counts to avoid false triggers.
5) Fast feedback loop. Rituals that surface human judgment within 15–60 minutes of anomaly detection.

Sentinel taxonomy (recommended):
- Safety/Behavioral sentinels (owner: ML/Product)
  - Hallucination proxy: fraction of responses flagged by QA heuristics or NLU classifier as 'low-fidelity' in a rolling 1h window (thresholds: warning >1% of sampled responses, critical >3% OR >50 events). Action: throttle rollout and run sample review.
  - Toxicity/explosive content: downstream classifier score >0.7 on >0.1% of responses. Action: immediate rollback of slice on critical, escalate to safety team.

- Quality/UX sentinels (owner: Product/Analytics)
  - Resolving rate: % of sessions where user marks item as 'resolved' or engages with the result. Drop >7% relative to baseline (7-day baseline) -> investigate prompt/temperature changes.
  - Latency impact on UX: % of requests with end-to-end latency >1s (or product-specific SLA). Increase of +15 percentile points over baseline -> reroute traffic to stable variant or increase pool capacity.

- Reliability/infra sentinels (owner: SRE)
  - Error rate: 5xx/total calls and decoder errors. Warning >0.5 percentage points absolute; Critical >2 percentage points OR >100 errors in 10 minutes. Action: fallback to lower-cost model and page SRE.
  - Token throttling/backpressure events: any sustained backpressure for >3 minutes -> immediate scaling policy evaluation and possible canary rollback.

- Cost/efficiency sentinels (owner: Platform/Product)
  - Token spend per session: median tokens/session increases >20% vs baseline AND cost delta >$X per 10k requests -> pause exposure and investigate prompt/behavioral change.

How to combine ratio + absolute checks (pattern):
- Use ratio triggers with a minimum event floor (e.g., hallucination rate >1% AND >=25 flagged responses in last 1h). This prevents noisy alerts on tiny slices.

Slice allocation heuristics (quick rules):
- Start very small: seed with 0.1% random traffic + 0.5% internal employee veterans.
- Incremental step sizes: doubles until 1% (0.1 -> 0.2 -> 0.5 -> 1), then +1–5% depending on risk appetite.
- Prefer stratified slices over purely random for skewed user bases: ensure at least one slice that is high-traffic/edge-case cohort (e.g., long prompts, high token average).
- Always reserve a shadow slice for synthetic traffic with deterministic prompts (see synthetic traffic below).

Synthetic traffic and test harnesses (must-run before any exposure)
- Golden prompt set: 120 prompts that exercise common success cases and critical failure modes (QA, hallucination, safety boundaries). Run these every deployment and after each step.
- Stress generator: short-burst high-concurrency tests to validate autoscaler and backpressure behavior for the slice.
- Canary-only adversarial suite: prompts designed to push hallucination/safety model boundaries; failures escalate to immediate rollback.

Observation rituals (who does what and when)
- Pre-launch (T-48 to T-1)
  - Product: confirm hypothesis and success metrics (primary and 2–3 secondary sentinels).
  - ML: run golden prompt set and compare logits/PD metrics vs baseline.
  - SRE: validate autoscale and traffic routing, run smoke synthetic traffic.
  - Ops ticket created with runbook link and primary/secondary on-call.

- Hour-0 (first 60 minutes after first exposure) — 'Hour-1 ritual'
  - Frequency: live check-ins at 5', 15', 30', 60'.
  - Owners: product + SRE + ML presence in the call or shared slack channel.
  - Actions: check sentinel panel (top 8 sentinels), sample 10 responses per slice, confirm no critical safety or unrecoverable infra events.

- Day-0 to Day-1
  - 3x observation sweeps (2h, 6h, 24h).
  - Small review doc where product lists interesting user-visible behaviors (notes to follow up).

- 72h to 7d
  - Drift review at 72h and at 7 days: compare sentinel deltas vs baseline. If persistent deviation >30% for primary sentinel, escalate to rollback planning.

Escalation ladder (concrete actions)
- Sentinel WARNING: post to rollout channel, tag stakeholders, increase sampling for manual review, add short synthetic run.
- Sentinel SEVERE: stop further ramping, reroute new traffic to baseline variant, page SRE if infra; product/ML ASSESS in 30 min.
- Sentinel CRITICAL: immediate rollback of the slice, open incident with SLA RRT (response timeframe), require postmortem within 72h.

Playbook snippets (copy/paste for runbooks)
- "If hallucination proxy >3% AND >=50 flagged responses in last 60m: set canary percentage to 0, enable rollout fallback to model-v1, and collect 200 samples for ML triage. Notify #prod-canary and tag @ml-lead."
- "If 5xx spike >100 errors in 10m: set traffic weight for canary to 0 and trigger SRE page. Record logs: request_id, model_version, host_pool, seq_len"

Sampling guidance for manual inspection
- Always do a stratified 10-sample: 5 top-quality, 3 edge-case (long/punctuated), 2 random. Record verdicts in the canary notes doc (pass/fail with short rationale).

Dashboards and panels (minimum)
- Cross-slice sentinel view (showing each slice as a row, sentinels as columns).
- Detail panel per slice with time-series for each sentinel and links to raw sample lists.
- Synthetic golden run results and per-deployment diffs.

Open questions / TODOs
- TODO: settle exact token-cost threshold ($X) for cost-sentinel escalation for hosted vs dedicated customers. (Action: finance + pricing to propose.)
- TODO: integrate a lightweight manual triage app so reviewers can tag samples and feed that back into ML classifier training. (ENG-3421)
- Question: how to encode multi-variant experiments where traffic is split across more than two models? Proposal: require sentinel owners for each model and an aggregate sentinel that compares vector of deltas.

Appendix A — Sentinel template (one-line form to paste into docs):
- Name | Owner | Metric definition | Window | Floor | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Action(s) | Pager? | Link to dashboard
  - Example: Hallucination proxy | ML-Quality | % flagged by QA classifier / sampled responses | 60m | 25 events | >1% | >3% OR >=50 events | Pause rollout, collect samples, manual triage | No (pager at critical) | <dash link>

Appendix B — Quick checklist for on-call during canary
- Acknowledge canary channel and set quiet hours for noise reduction.
- Verify autoscaler is healthy and there are no recent deploys to infra components.
- Run synthetic golden set and confirm no regressions.
- Perform the Hour-1 10-sample manual check.

Notes to self / context snippets (informal):
- We want a shared vocabulary so product doesn't panic at every 0.2% change and SRE isn't buried in false positives.
- Keep the sentinel list intentionally small; teams can add experimental metrics but these should not auto-page.
- This doc is a working draft — aim to land on a canonical sentinel dashboard with enforced floor/rate thresholds in the console by Q2.

Links and references
- Confluence: traffic slicing design (linked above).
- GH: console canary routing PR (linked above).
- Jira: ENG-3421 (triage app), ML-590 (golden prompt set maintenance).

If you're reading this and have a strong opinion on the hallucination proxy thresholds, ping me (Priya) and we'll slot a 30m sync with ML quality and product on Monday.
